## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hiri Sutta* (or *Hirisutta*, Snp 2.3) is a discourse found in the *Cūḷavagga* of the *Suttanipāta* [SuttaCentral; Müller 1881]. Its primary theme is how to recognize a true friend [SuttaCentral]. In delineating authentic friendship, the text employs a striking simile of the maternal bond: a genuine friend is not someone who constantly suspects a breach or looks for faults, but one with whom a person can dwell securely as a son at his mother's breast, forming a bond that cannot easily be severed by others [Tsomo 1999; Müller 1881]. The sutta also extols the sweetness of seclusion and tranquility, noting that drinking in the sweetness of the Dhamma frees one from fear and fault [Müller 1881].

In the traditional commentary, the *Paramatthajotikā*, the *Hirisuttavaṇṇanā* provides detailed commentary on the discourse, including an exposition of eight classes of ascetics (*tāpasas*), such as *Saputtabhariyā*, *Uñchācārikā*, *Sampattakālikā*, and others [Sarao and Long 2017].

A full parallel to the sutta is preserved in the *Hirijātaka* (Ja 363) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this close correspondence, detecting extensive shared verse sequences between the *Hiri Sutta* and both Ja 363 (§0.2–5.5) and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, individual verses have parallels across Buddhist literature, including verse-level parallels in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 205), the *Vaṇṇārohajātaka* (Ja 361), and multiple recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 28, UVS 28, Uv Kg 28, T 212, and T 213) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus also records machine-generated cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99 and T 100) [DharmaNexus].
